properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25: *"I forget how big you said the reflow2 project json file is, but I believe it was 50+ MB? I can't remember, but github has a size restriction for files that can be git pushed (I believe a hard limitation is 100 MiB). Hence, compressing the file discussion"* — with minification, gzip/zstd/brotli and key-shortening laid out as the options.

**THE INSTINCT TO LOOK WAS RIGHT AND EVERY NUMBER CAME OUT DIFFERENT FROM THE GENERIC ADVICE.** All measured 2026-08-25 at main `691b4fb`.

═══ 1. THE FILE IS NOT NEAR THE LIMIT ═══

    raw (pretty-printed)      8.32 MB    ← 8.3% of GitHub's 100 MiB hard limit
    GitHub hard limit        100.00 MiB    ~12x headroom

The 50+ MB recollection is about 6x high. **There is no file-size problem to solve.**

═══ 2. ⚠️ MINIFICATION BUYS 12%, NOT 40-80% — AND THE REASON GENERALISES ═══

    minified (jq -c)          7.34 MB    88.2% of raw   →  1.1x
    gzip -9                   2.11 MB    25.3%          →  3.9x
    minified + gzip           2.06 MB    24.8%          →  4.0x
    zstd -19                  1.27 MB    15.3%          →  6.6x

The standard "40-80%" figure assumes machine-generated records: short values, many repeated keys, deep structural syntax. **reflow2's export is the exact inverse.** Measured composition:

    string VALUES   5.95 MB   78.5%   ← the prose
    KEY names       0.97 MB   12.8%   ← all that key-shortening could ever touch

⇒ **Key-shortening has a 12.8% ceiling and would break every reader** — the schema, the Python gates, `compare_designs`, every consumer. Converting to a header+matrix form has the same ceiling for the same reason.

═══ 3. ⭐⭐ COMMITTING IT COMPRESSED WOULD MAKE THE REPOSITORY BIGGER, MEASURED ═══

What git ACTUALLY spends on 550 revisions of this path:

    revisions                    550
    sum of logical sizes    1,729.3 MB
    actual on-disk cost       357.0 MB   (20.64% — delta + zlib)
    AVERAGE PER REVISION      664.6 KB

Compare a per-file compressor: gzip -9 is **2.11 MB**, zstd -19 is **1.27 MB**. Git already beats both by 2-3x, because successive exports of one design are ENORMOUSLY similar and delta-compress against each other.

🛑 **A COMPRESSED BLOB HAS NO EXPLOITABLE SIMILARITY TO THE PREVIOUS COMPRESSED BLOB.** Commit `.json.zst` and every revision costs its full ~1.27 MB instead of 664 KB. **The proposal that looks like it saves 85% actually costs about 2x** — and it destroys `git diff` on the one artifact whose diff a reviewer most needs to read.

═══ 4. REFORMATTING IS SAFE FOR THE LINEAGE, WHICH WAS WORTH CHECKING ═══

`compute_content_hash` is sha256 over the **canonical compact sorted-key JSON of `{edges, graph_id, nodes}`** — the design content, NOT the file bytes. So pretty-printing, minifying or reformatting does not move `content_hash` and cannot sever the chain. **The objection that would have killed minification outright does not apply.** (It still destroys diff readability, which is a different and larger objection.)

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. DO NOTHING.** 8.3% of the file limit; `.git` is 539 MB, of which 357 MB is this path's history.
 ⚠️ Grows ~65 MB per 100 PRs. Fine for years; not free forever.

**B. MINIFY BEFORE COMMIT.** 12% smaller.
 ⚠️ Turns a 136,374-line file into ONE line. Every design diff becomes "the file changed" — and the design diff is what a reviewer reads to see what a PR did to the model. **12% for the loss of reviewability is the worst trade on this list.**

**C. COMPRESS BEFORE COMMIT (gzip/zstd/brotli).** ❌ **MEASURED WORSE**: ~2x the repository, plus no diff at all.

**D. COMMIT THE EXPORT LESS OFTEN.** The repo cost is 550 revisions × 664 KB, not the file size. Export on release, or on demand, rather than once per PR.
 ⭐ The only option that attacks the measured driver. ⚠️ It collides head-on with `dec:export-once-per-pr` and with the export being the reviewable record of a PR — and it interacts with the store-inversion work, where the export becomes the DURABLE copy and wants writing MORE often, not less. Those two pull in opposite directions and that tension is the real content here.

**E. ATTACK THE PROSE.** 78.5% is string values; `decision` 16.0%, `statement` 14.7%, `rationale` 6.3%, `description` 6.1% — **43% of the document in four fields.**
 ⚠️ AND THIS IMPLICATES HOW THE GRAPH IS WRITTEN, INCLUDING BY THIS AGENT: single statements of 3,000+ characters were written today. The prose is the value of the design — it is the reasoning that would otherwise be lost — so "write less" is not obviously right. But it IS where the bytes are, and nobody has ever asked whether the marginal paragraph earns its place.

**F. HISTORY-LEVEL TOOLS** — Git LFS, shallow clones, periodic history rewrite.
 ⚠️ LFS makes the design un-diffable and un-reviewable in the web UI; rewriting history breaks every existing clone and hash reference.

📌 THE FRAME THAT MAY MATTER MORE THAN ANY OPTION: this asks about the ARCHIVAL copy at the moment the project is deciding whether the export becomes the DURABLE copy (`dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth`). Measured the same day: a separate gitignored autosave path dissolves the auto-export/lineage collision. **If durability moves to a path git never sees, then how often the ARCHIVAL copy is committed becomes a free variable** — and option D stops fighting the export-once-per-PR rule.
properties.name: OPEN — the export is 8.3 MB, not 50; minifying buys 12%, and committing it COMPRESSED would make the repo 2-3x BIGGER. The cost is 550 committed revisions and the prose inside them, not the encoding
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill as an idea, not intent, and linked on creation.

Every figure was measured rather than taken from the general advice, and that turned out to matter three times: the file is 6x smaller than remembered, minification is 6x weaker than the standard estimate because this document is prose rather than records, and compressing before commit is not a saving at all but roughly a doubling. **A brainstorm that had reasoned from the generic numbers would have recommended exactly the wrong thing.**

The options are kept with their costs rather than ranked, because the choice turns on something not settled yet — whether the export is about to become the durable copy, which changes what the committed copy is even for.
